utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Di Fazio, before we start, I'll just inform -- let's go into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I think the curtains of the public gallery may be opened. Security is instructed not to allow anyone else in the public gallery. Mr. Di Fazio, are you ready to continue the examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so, I'd like to remind you, Witness, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, perhaps just before I do, can I say that on my left is Mr. Phil Carney, who I omitted to introduce to you yesterday, and I extend my apologies both to Mr. Carney and to this Trial Chamber. Mr. Carney is an experienced attorney from the United States and the Prosecution is very pleased to have him on board, and I thought it best that I ought to formally introduce him to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Welcome, Mr. Carney.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARNEY
utterances.text: Members of the panel, good morning. It's a pleasure and honour to be here with colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday I was asking you some questions about sister S, and you described for us the night that your house was visited by these men and how your mother reported to you the episode of what had happened. Can I just ask you this: Were you awake or aware of the men being in your house that night, even though you may not have seen who they were and what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asleep in the other room with my brothers, and I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. The next morning when you woke up, was sister S in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you -- did you see her again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a short while, she was brought back to the house for a visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you try and give the Trial Chamber some assistance with the period of time. You said "a short while." Now, is that a matter of hours, days, a week or a month? Can you assist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about a week later when she was brought for a visit. It was warm, I would say. Maybe it was summer, something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how did she get back to your house? How did she make her way back to the family home on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Togeri and two or three soldiers brought her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see this on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How were they dressed? I mean Togeri and the two or three soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in black uniforms with the KLA insignia, and they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thinking back, about how long did they remain at your house on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say from 20 minutes to half an hour, as far as I remember. It wasn't a long visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how did they arrive at the house? Was it on horseback or foot or vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came by a jeep. It was a black jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, had you ever seen that black jeep before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not often. I have seen it sometimes because they used different cars. I didn't see the same car often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And on this occasion, where did the men who brought your sister S back, where did they stay during the 20 minutes or half an hour? Did they come inside the house, in the garden, stay in the car? What precisely did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two or three others remained near the car. Togeri came to the yard with my sister. We invited him in. We offered something to drink to him, and he stayed there during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he masked or did he have anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how long did you lay eyes on him? Was it for the full 20 minutes or half hour or a shorter period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you hear him speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that the first time that you heard him speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you have a chance to speak to your sister, sister S, alone; that is, not in the presence of Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. She was with them and we talked. He came in for a short time and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She came into the house for a short time and then left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And did he take the refreshment that was offered to him by your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you remember what he said? If you can't, don't tell us, but if you can remember what he said, please, I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what he said, but we couldn't speak as we wished with our sister other than exchanging the usual pleasantries, How you are, and so on. So we were all together all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And how was your sister dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was dressed in the KLA uniform, black clothes. She had the same uniform as them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P9, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look at that insignia that you see there. Have you seen that before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the KLA emblem or insignia that they wore all the time during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yesterday and today, you've described insignia on uniforms. Is that the sort of insignia you saw on uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the same. The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It can be taken off the screen, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your sister provide any explanation to your family as to what she was doing with this KLA, why she was dressed in black uniform? Did she have a chance to give you any explanation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because she was ordered not to tell us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How do you know that? How do you know that she was ordered not to tell you anything? Is that something you concluded yourself or is it something that you know, you got some information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard from my mother, when she asked her about something, my sister had retorted, Don't ask me anything because I'm not supposed to tell you anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, she eventually left. Did she leave in company with Togeri and the other KLA men in the black jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see sister S again following this first visit back home, back to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw her another time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, try and give us an idea of how long after this first visit back she came back again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably one or two weeks after the first visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Before we get on to the second visit, I want to know, did your family make any attempts to contact her or find out what was going on? Are you aware -- can you recall any such attempts? If you can't recall, say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if we contacted the sister after she was taken away by the Togeri?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. In between the first visit that she -- indeed, at any time leading up to -- during -- following the period of time that she was taken away and the first and second visits, did you and your family make any attempts to find out what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, let's focus your attention on this second visit when your sister came back. Again, how did she arrive at -- how did she make her way to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was brought by Togeri and two soldiers for a visit. They were in a Niva, white Niva car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you recall any unusual feature about the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first -- it had only the first glass window, the windscreen it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did it have a roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The windscreen? It was a white Niva. It was a convertible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And on this occasion, how was Toger -- how were Toger and the two soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in the same black uniform with the KLA insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we just go into private session briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that Toger and the soldiers came to your house in the convertible Niva. On this occasion, did your sister S have any time alone with the family or were Toger and the two soldiers around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They brought her for a visit, and they went back. They didn't stay at home. It was about 10.00 in the morning, as far as I remember, and she remained with us for about two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did she tell you or did you hear her tell your family members what she was doing? By that, I mean what she was doing with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because Toger had instructed her not to mention anything about what was going on there because otherwise she would have problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, can you tell the Trial Chamber how you know that? How do you know that Toger had issued these instructions? Just hang on a minute before you answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm rising for the standing objection of hearsay and understand, of course, the Court's ruling and understand the Court's concern with the flow of testimony, so in this regard it will be a continuing objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We already took that as a given fact, since you yesterday also -- so there's no need to repeat that. It's understood that you, Mr. Guy-Smith, that you object against whatever question soliciting hearsay evidence from the witness. Mr. Di Fazio. And I should say it's rejected, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You just testified earlier that Toger had instructed her not to mention anything about what was going on "because otherwise she would have problems." What I want to know is how do you know that? What's your source of information? How do you -- why do you make that claim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because when we were with my sister and when mom was asking her, How are you doing, what are you doing there, she had replied to my mother, Don't ask me such questions for which I can give you no answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In all the time that your sister was living --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, could we please further explore that because it's not -- it's half an answer to your question. May I ask you, you earlier said that Toger had instructed your sister, and then Mr. Di Fazio asked you how you knew and then you said, Well, when my mother asked her certain matters, she said, Don't ask me such questions for which I can give you no answer. That in itself is not a reason for you to know that your sister was instructed and by whom she was instructed. Did she just say, Don't ask me matters I can't answer, or did she further specify, in line with your earlier testimony, who told her and therefore that it was not her own opinion that she shouldn't answer but that she was instructed, and by whom she was instructed not to talk about these matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is true? Now, I'm trying to find out what exactly -- did your sister just say, Don't ask questions, I can't answer, or did she give any specifics as whether she was instructed; and if so, by whom she was instructed not to speak about these matters? What did your sister say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My sister said to mom, Don't ask me anything about what I am involved in because I'm afraid to tell you. If I tell you, I'm afraid something bad will happen to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, I understand that she didn't say that she was, as your earlier testimony was, that she was instructed by Toger not to say anything, but she said, Don't ask me because it will not be good for me. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She didn't say explicitly that Toger had told her. She simply said what I already told you, that I cannot speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honour -- I'm just reading the transcript, Your Honour. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've said that when she was brought -- you may not have said this, and I apologise if I'm revisiting old testimony, but when she was first brought to the house by Toger and the others in the Niva, the convertible Niva, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When your sister was in the house for those two or three hours with your family, was she armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. She was dressed in uniform, a black uniform, with a KLA insignia and she had handcuffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What do you mean "handcuffs"? She was handcuffed or she had handcuffs in her possession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had some thumbcuffs, not handcuffs, and they were hanging there on the belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. But apart from handcuffs, did she have any guns, any pistols, grenades, automatic rifles, any form of armament at all apart from the cuffs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she had nothing else. She only had these cuffs and the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what her demeanour was like? By that, I mean did she appear -- what was her emotional state? How did it appear to you? Did she appear to be happy?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection; leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps the second part of the question may be falling into error, so I'll just ask the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber what her state was like when she was at your house during those two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to describe it. As far as talking is concerned, she talked in a normal manner, and even if she had seen something terrible, she pretended that everything was okay. She didn't let us know whether she was happy or not happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had she mentioned at any time a desire to join the KLA? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that she said, I have become a KLA member, that Toger was a superior to her, a kind of commander, and that she would follow his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Now, apart from that and apart from what she said on this visit, had she ever expressed to you or any member of your family on any previous occasion any ambition or desire to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had any other member of your family, as far as you're aware, ever express an ambition or desire to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection; relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that Toger said that she had to become a KLA member and she became a KLA member, but I don't remember any member of my family telling her to become a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would interpose the other objection. The members of the family that exist are relatively young in age, which is the reason that I interpose the relevance objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, as a matter of fact, "members of the family" is a rather wide expression, and you made your objection and I overruled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm happy to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. There is another matter which I'd like to draw your attention to, Mr. Di Fazio. The witness was not answering your question, so that's perhaps that's the first thing we should try to elicit from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if any member of your family told her, told sister S, to join the KLA, I'm asking you a different question. My question is this: Did any member of your family, and particularly your older brothers and sisters, ever express a desire or ambition to join the KLA? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't want to join because they were scared, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've said your sister stayed at the house, I think, for about two or three hours on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the second visit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We're talking now about the second visit. How did she eventually leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon, my brother escorted her to the place where she had to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I just forgot to switch off my microphone when the witness was answering the question. I see that you're following this bad habit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I had been doing rather well. I need to know the name of the brother, and I think we need to go into private session for that question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you have any idea where your brother was taking or going with sister S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my sister was under the order to return to the base where she had been previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to where that base was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a place called Irzniq. It's a village or a townlet, but it's called Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And about how far from your village is that, approximately? See if you can give us an idea in terms of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably 4 or 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, would you please further explore the source of knowledge in relation to the order to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Yes, that does need clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You told the Court that your sister was under the order to return to the base. Again, what's your source of information for making that assertion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When she came that morning for a visit, she said that Toger had told her to return to the base where she had been previously at that particular hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, in view of the previous answer, you said she told you that "Toger had told her to return. Did she use these words? Did she mention the name as the person who had told her to return or did she say, I am told to return? I'm just seeking to verify the precision of the answer you gave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She mentioned the name of this person Togeri in the context that he had told her that, You have to be back at this particular hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when she left your home, which direction was she walking in? I know you've said that she was with your brother. Which direction were they both walking in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Irzniq, the place where she was supposed to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any other soldiers that day, and after they left, walking in the direction of Rznic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see two or three soldiers who came in a Niva car with the windscreen only. They asked us, Where is your sister? And we told them that she set off to return to the place where she was told to return. And then they left at top speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the soldiers in the Niva on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised one of them. It was Togeri with another soldier or two soldiers. He asked, Where is your sister? And we told them that my brother is escorting her, and they left immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us now of two occasions when you saw Toger on this day, when he brought your sister -- when he accompanied your sister to your house and on this occasion when he came back. On that day, did you hear him speak? Did you hear his voice? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was with my mother and with the small brother outside the house in the garden. I think the distance was 3 or 4 metres between us. We told him that my sister had set off, and he then left immediately. He didn't wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And earlier in the day when your sister had arrived, did you hear him speak on that occasion? Did you hear his voice on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And thinking back now, I know it's quite some time ago, but thinking back now, how long would you say you laid eyes on him altogether that day? Remember, you've told us that you saw him when he came with your sister and later when he came to make inquiries after she'd left. Now, taking into account those two occasions, how long did you have an opportunity to look at him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these two occasions, I saw him pretty often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, I think you misunderstand. I'll ask you again. I'm not asking about other occasions, I'm asking about this day that sister S came back to the house, okay? On that day, on that day only, for how long did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's okay, no problem. But on that day, for how long did you see Toger, both taking into account the time when he first came to the house and when he left -- sorry, and when he came back, asking about your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came for the second time to look for my sister and when my sister had left, I saw him -- that was the last time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Have you ever seen your sister again, sister S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So when she walked off with your brother, you never saw her again. Are you aware of any other member of your family ever seeing her again after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment that she walked off, none of us saw her again, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You may have told us this already, but I'd just like to ask you again. How old was she at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-three, 24, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I would like the witness to -- just before this is done, I assume that this image is not going to go out to the public. I want to make sure of that. Thank you. I'd like the witness to be shown 65 ter 685, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number .

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit number P16, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who are those people?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who's the lady on the left dressed with the longer crimson or dark red dress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my mom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I'm grateful to my case manager. I realise we need to redact this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you should have instructed the witness not to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I realise that. I omitted to do so, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that what she looked like? Is that what sister S looked like when you last saw her; that she had that sort of look, that length of hair and about that age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with this hair, with that length of hair at that age. I am not sure she was of this particular age that I see her here, but she had this look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I tender the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections. Therefore, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your family continued to live in the village, in the house, following this occasion when sister S left to go back to Rznic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your mother continued to live at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: She had been, of course, wounded and she'd come out of hospital. Was she able to get around or was she still recovering from her wounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yesterday, you described occasions when KLA soldiers would come to your house searching for weapons. Following this occasion when sister S -- when you last saw sister S, did any further visits of that nature occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my sister left, whom we didn't see anymore, a considerable period of time passed and then we started to have visits again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what would happen during these visits? And I want to know these -- listen to the question. I want to know these features: I want to know who came on these visits, what they might have been wearing, carrying, times of the visits, and also frequency of the visits. How often did these visits take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened that they came three, four times a week, sometimes every two days, sometimes once a week. But these visits were very frequent, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, who came on the visits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them I knew; he was Togeri. The others wore masks. Toger, too, had a mask, but he had rolled it up and I could see his face so I could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you specifically about Togeri, but I'm just asking you generally now about the visits which you say occurred fairly frequently. Who was it who came on these visits? Is it your position that Togeri was always there, or sometimes there, or once or twice? Can you give us an idea, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him when he had his mask rolled up on top of his head. The others I couldn't recognise because they kept their masks on. And I was very young, I was very scared. I didn't want to be very attentive, so to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I don't think that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection; non-responsive. Move to strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand -- I'm not quite sure what that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- but let me see whether I understand it. I think that Mr. Guy-Smith says that it's not a response to the question; therefore, it should be stricken from the record and not to be taken into consideration at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct. And I'm specifically dealing with the issue of the frequency of the visits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me reread it. You say you're talking about the frequency, but that was in the previous answer already, Mr. Guy-Smith, or am I mistaken? Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As I'm reading the record, Your Honour, looking at the question starting on line 9: "I'm going to ask you specifically about Togeri, but I'm just asking you generally ... about the visits that you say occurred fairly frequently," and the balance of that answer deals with the frequency of the visits. His answer does not deal with the question propounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, we will not strike it from the record. If it was not a response to a question, it certainly would have been a response to questions I would have in this respect, so, therefore, to that extent, it is responsive to a question not yet put to the witness, and I even have another question in this matter, and since we're dealing with it now, I'll put it to the witness right away. You said about these visits that that was after a certain period of time. Could you describe -- when you said then the visits started again and were frequent, and then you mentioned how often a week, could you tell us how long there were no visits? Once your sister left for the last time your house, you said during a period of time they did not come. Could you say was that a week? Was that a month? Was that three months? Was that a year? Could you further explain to us how long a period that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably a month. I'm not very certain when we had two or three visits during the day, but usually the visits were at night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's not what I asked. You said once your sister had left, during a certain period of time there were no visits, from what I remember. Let me just check. I'll read your answer. I would like to know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After a month, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So after a month the visits started again, approximately, after a month that your sister had left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, it was about a month that the visits started to become more frequent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I will first read again the answer you gave to one of the previous questions. You said: "After my sister left, whom we didn't see anymore, a considerable period of time passed and then we started to have visits again." I understood this to be that during this considerable period of time, that there were no visits at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe about a month, it was the period during which we didn't have visits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said the visits started again. Were they, on from the beginning, frequent visits again or was it with a low frequency that went up at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They started gradually and then after a brief period of time, these visits became more frequent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say a brief period of time, so one month no visits, then a period of visits not being frequent? When, after how much time, they became frequent again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The visits started about two, three, months later, when they became very frequent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The request was rejected, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. And I apologise for the move to strike part of my objection. I was relying on days gone by. The balance of my objection, however, I did intend. I won't move to strike anything else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've told us about frequency of visits, and it's been explored and we've heard what you've got to say. What I'd like to know is this: Whenever the visits occurred, were the men armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every time they came, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were all or some of the men in uniform; and if so, what sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many times I saw them in black uniforms. Most of them, I would say almost every time, they were wearing black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did these uniforms have the insignia that I showed to you earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about your mother but in a while. I'm talking about the period of time between the last time you saw sister S and something that happened to your mother. I'm talking about that period of time. During this period of time, you've testified -- you've said that there were visits, and you've described already how often and when they happened. During these visits, did you ever see Toger, or Togeri? I'm not asking you about anything relating to your mother; I'm just talking about these frequent visits that you've mentioned. Now, during these frequent visits that you've spoken about, did you ever see Togeri, or is it the case that you did not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were occasions when I didn't see him; there were occasions when I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And on the occasions that these men came to your house, were they masked or not? These are the frequent visits I'm talking about now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were masked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So if, during these frequent visits the men were masked, how is it that you saw Togeri?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Di Fazio, the witness has answered that question. He told us that this mask was rolled up from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that evidence, Your Honour. I'm just -- I just want to be absolutely certain that that's what the witness was saying. I'm a little bit unclear and I think should that be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You heard what His Honour had to say. You've told us these things --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- on frequent visits, some of the visits Toger was there. You've also mentioned that you recall him raising his mask. Now, my question is this: During these frequent visits, when Toger -- on the occasions that Toger was there, did he -- is that when he raised his mask and you saw his face? That's what I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have to object to the form of the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think he can get to the information in a more appropriate fashion. I'm not objecting, of course, to him seeking this information whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has now -- I think the question has been put to the witness three times. Mr. Di Fazio is seeking -- you earlier testified about Toger, or Togeri, putting up his mask, at least that you were in a position to see his face. Could you tell us whether that happened all the times when you saw him visiting your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Very rarely. So when there was a big problem with my family, then he would roll up his mask, but he didn't do this very often. He would roll up his mask very rarely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if he did not roll up his mask, how would you know that Togeri was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When his mask was not raised, I wasn't in a position to tell whether it was him or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you say that he was present, although not ever, are you telling us that at those occasions where you say he was present that he rolled up his mask, and that other occasions he may have been there but you are not able to see his face and, therefore, you cannot confirm his presence? Is that how we should understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible that he was there, but I wasn't able to recognise him if he had his mask on. And I was young. I was scared. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that you could not see his face but that you heard a voice which you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The voice sounded familiar, but I cannot tell you that it was him. I'm not absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours, that's covered that topic, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm getting the French on channel 4. I apologise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After some time, maybe after three or four months --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, earlier I think we tried to explain to you why we went into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think this is going to identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I do. I do understand. I didn't think this would cause the problem, but certainly from an abundance of caution, perhaps it's best if we go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you some very brief questions about the trip. Tell the Trial Chamber which way you went to get from your village to Glodjane in order to carry out this inquiry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went towards Irzniq - that's the name of the village - and then we took a mountain path. When we arrived there, we came across three or four soldiers, and when they asked us, Where are you going, we said to them, Well, we've heard that there is a prison and (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) And then we decided to go back home and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P10. Thank you. And could we just focus in on -- a bit more on the centre of the map, to the north of the lake. Yes, that's precisely what I want, thank you. And may I seek the assistance of the usher?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, a wonder of modern technology, on the -- you've got a pen on the side of the screen there, and you can -- by touching the screen, don't touch the screen yet, but by using the pen you can indicate the path you took. Can you just show the Trial Chamber the path that you took and mark it with the special red pen, please, by just touching the screen and show the Judges which way you went to get to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have to find my village first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Shouldn't we enlarge that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful to Your Honour. That might assist. Could we perhaps get it a little bit bigger? That's a bit too big.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all, can you see the lake there? Can you see the lake depicted on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just look above that. I think you'll see your village there. A little bit of the way up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see two villages here, the upper and the lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. And I think if you look over to the left, you'll see Rznic. Just mark on that map, using the magic pen, and show the Trial Chamber which way you went to get to ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately this is the direction that we took from Ratis e Ulet to Ratis e Eperme, but I cannot find where Irzniq is. I can't see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just look to the left of the image. Look to the left, look to the left. I think you'll see Rznic there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If there's no objection to this, can I approach the witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My problem is that I, until now, have never heard the R in the spelling of the village. So let us first try to verify whether that -- whether your assumption because that -- is it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness might remove his headphones just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 19, would you take off your headphones for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is simply on geography, if I may, and it may serve to avoid confusion later on. There is a town called Istinic, with an S, which is north of the location shown on this map. It's not shown on this map. It's further north. And then there's a town in Irzniq, which in Serbian begins with an R, but in Albanian begins with an I, but the emphasis is on "znic". So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that could well be what we find on the map as Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Rznic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, that's close. So, therefore, you say it's likely when I heard, until now, a word not starting with an R, that is understandable if you look at the Albanian spelling of this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All that I'm saying, just for clarification, is that Rznic and Irzniq are respectively the Serbian and Albanian names for the village that one sees to the left of the map. But there is a separate town of Istinic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which is easily confused to the ear, which is further north. Indeed, it was a place that I mentioned in my opening speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, the witness says that he went to Glodjane, and if it's not on the map, not even on the larger map, I do understand this, then, of course, it would be -- well, not the shortest route to Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm deliberately refraining from commenting on this witness's evidence or what he's saying. I leave that to be explored by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. Could the witness please put his headphones on again. Witness, we are a bit confused by names of villages. You earlier said, and I'll find it on the transcript ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you have the words in capital -- the letters in capital G and D, which refer to Gornji, upper, or "e Eperme" in Albanian, and Donji, lower, or "e Poshtme" in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation, but that's not exactly what our problem was. I'm just trying to see where ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain it in my own words, the route that we took?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But first, please, you'll answer my question. You earlier said: "I cannot find where Irzniq is." That's what we read on the transcript. Now, we see a village on the screen which is called Rznic, which is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Rznic, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that the same village, but spelled a bit differently, as the village you earlier referred to which you called Irzniq? When you said Irzniq --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's called Irzniq, but here it is written Rznic, which is the same village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That has been clarified now. Then, yes, please explain further what route you took when you went to Glodjane. You can use the pen since you have now found Rznic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ratis e Ulet is Ratis with the D in front or with a G, because there are two parts of Ratis village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you able to further mark your route on the map, or do you find that difficult?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I want to know whether Ratis e Eperme is the one with the G or with the D letter in front?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you, but is there any objection if Mr. Di Fazio assists the witness in at least a starting point?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, given the time limitations, for the purposes of our case, I think I've gone as far as I need to, or can, with this matter and I need to move on. I don't need to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I take it that you are not going to tender the marked map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then it did not yet receive a number until now, so it's -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned earlier in your testimony sister M. Did she continue to live with your family (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. When my sister was taken away, she continued to live with us until the day she disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think we need to go into private session, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did they get into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night we were asleep at around 10.30 when they came. The door, while I was asleep, was broken down. They entered the house. They were wearing masks, and they had flashlights in their hands. They told us to get up, and they put us against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I want to show some images to the witness. Can the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these images to be tendered for admission under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, they might identify -- they have the tendency to identify the witness, and so therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they should not be shown on any screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In relation to the photograph you showed earlier, you did not specifically ask for it to be tendered under seal, but due to the testimony and the content of the photograph, it was admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour. I'm sorry I overlooked that. I certainly ask that these be tendered under seal. Firstly, can the witness be shown 65 ter 1187.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P17, marked for identification and under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's not the image that I want.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Don't make any comments.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for all the assistance that I've got this morning from the court officers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, have a look at that place. It's clearly in ruins now, but do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, I take it? It's admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just want to -- for the assistance of the court officers, I'm going to show a number of images of this building, and I just briefly want to show them as fast as I can and ask the witness to identify them, and then I'll ask some questions. So could the witness now be shown 65 ter 1181.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us, is that -- what is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A number for this one would be, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And just to finally confirm, Witness, do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. What is it? Is that your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I seek to tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is no objection, but I would request that the Prosecution refrain from leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That was leading, I know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is leading, Mr. Guy-Smith. What is the rationale against leading? That is that you are suggesting something to the witness that would not have come into his mind and that putting, formulating, the question in this way that you lead him to a certain answer. Now, to be quite honest, many questions, of course, are leading. If you would eliminate all leading from questions, just add 200 per cent to the time you need for the witness. Now, to object against leading if you seem -- I don't know whether you accept that, we'll hear that, but let's just for the time being assume that this is the owner's house. You show some of the pictures of the owner of his house by saying, Was this your house, and, Oh, that had not come into my mind yet. Let's think about the rationale against leading and let's keep the objections specifically there where the rationale against leading is really influencing the witness. Of course, if you say no, that this wasn't his house, then we'll hear of that. But this would be the -- however leading it may be, it would be the -- it would be a question I would last object to as leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate the Court's observations and, in a general sense, don't disagree with the Court as it relates to this specific issue. However, an examination of the transcript thus far shows to me there's been a phenomenal amount of leading, and it's a problem that occurs in any proceeding, and it's the habit of questioning -- and it's the habit of questioning that I'm concerned about. And I take well your suggestion with regard to the particular question that was leading and that I objected to as it relates to the specific concerns raised by the Chamber. It's the habit that we're falling into that I'm quite concerned about. I believe the Chamber wishes to receive testimony from the witnesses, not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you. And I seek to tender that particular image into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then it is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: But let me ask, did the witness mean that this was the same house as the one we saw before or a different house? We saw two pictures now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, the same came into my mind. You asked the witness whether he recognised the house, the previous one. He said yes, which leads us without any knowledge as -- about the house, the structure, which leaves us without any knowledge on what that structure is. Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Not really, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you show the witness the house of his grandmother and says, Do you recognise that, the witness says yes, I still do not know whether it's his house, his grandmother's house, or the neighbour's house; so, therefore, that question was missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The images that I've shown you, all of the images of structures that I've shown you in the last few minutes, what does it depict? I know it shows a house, but whose house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the house of my family, where we used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And is this the house to which the KLA soldiers would -- came during these visits that you've described earlier in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just want to show the witness one more image, please. That would be 65 ter 1186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number P19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Earlier in your testimony today you said that the door was kicked in on this latest visit that you were describing. Can you see the door in that photograph, the door that you referred to earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness may need the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like you please, if you could, to mark on that photograph, using the red pen, where the door is that you talk about, the one that was kicked in. Show -- just draw a ring around it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 7

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about which door in the house? Is there any issue involved? I'm looking to the Defence, because we could ask about the windows and -- but let's try to focus on what seems to be -- or is there, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If the witness could take his earphones off for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is indication in the disclosure that we received that there are two doors in issue with regard to having been kicked in at some point in time. Other than that, with regard to anything else concerning the condition of the house, and by that I mean windows, roof, walls, or anything else, there's absolutely no dispute. I think with regard to the door there may be some question, but I'm not sure, depending on how this develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because this question now comes into my mind: I do not know -- we had a similar matter when another picture of two persons was shown and questions were asked as to whether that person looked, at a certain period, like on that picture. Is there any issue in relation to that, whether this -- or do we need further testimony to identify that person on that photograph? I'm just trying to find out what details we are exploring and whether they are details of matters which are in dispute or whether we're just getting the complete image. I mean, you could have shown to me any other house which might not have made that much of a difference for the case, unless --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't -- if Your Honours please, I'm not aware that the Defence are agreeing anything related -- concerning this particular body of evidence. I'm not aware of that. My soul purpose was to -- in showing this image to the witness was to provide Your Honours with a better understanding of his evidence. That was all that I intended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, a fairly honest question: Does the Prosecution think that if we would have been shown a different house with a different door that we would -- that that would have made any difference in our understanding of the testimony, apart from, again, whether there's a door issue or whether there's a door dispute? But the same for -- and I do understand that for the witness this is, of course, completely different, but if we would have seen a picture of two other persons, I mean, we know the age, would that have made any difference in understanding what this case is about and what this testimony is about? I'm just wondering what -- and whether one picture or three pictures makes it any better. I'm just trying to find out, and of course you could say if you continue to interrupt, then it will take more time. But I'm just trying to understand -- this Chamber will understand that if you kick in a door of a house, we all know what a door is, we all know what a house is, whether the house at this moment has a roof or has no roof, whether we've seen three pictures or one or none at all. That doesn't really matter unless there's any matter about doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first give Mr. Di Fazio an opportunity to respond because --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'm rather critical.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to lead evidence of eventual departure of this family from this area, and the reasons they did so is important for you to understand. This is an isolated place. You can see in these photographs for the first time, give you an idea of how isolated it was and the absolute terror that must have been inflicted on this family by these people coming to visit and the reasons why they left. This picture, it doesn't -- it won't add greatly, I fully admit that to Your Honours, to your understanding of the case, but it does depict that aspect of isolation that this family found itself in, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I tend to disagree with you on the basis of these photographs. I've got no idea how far the next-door neighbours are living, if it's 50 metres, whether it's 100 metres, whether it's 1 kilometre. I don't know. So to that extent, a question, where you were living, was that isolated and how far were the next-door neighbours? Living from there, would take you 20 seconds and we get the information where we need, rather than knowing where exactly in the house was the door that was kicked in. Forgive me when I'm a bit critical, but of course this is also in relation on the time used by the Prosecution, and it's also meant to be positive in contributing to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the use of time in court. Of course, we are no jury. I can imagine that in a jury trial that it's a bit different, but ... Okay, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If the Chamber needs a response to the questions asked, I've tried cases both in front of judges and juries. Based upon the colloquy that's just occurred and why Mr. Di Fazio apparently has tendered these particular photographs, I can assure you there will be no discussion or cross-examination with regard to the condition of doors and with regard to the photographs that were previously shown. I do not intend to ask any questions about those matters either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on. Could we ask the witness to put his earphones on again? I'd like to add to what I just said, because this is a public hearing as well, that where I was rather critical, that there's one thing I do understand and that is that in a public hearing, that apart from making it possible for the Judges to make their determinations they will have to make at a certain moment, that, of course, there's a public element involved as well. I'm not ignoring that, not at all, but whether we need the door to be marked on the building is -- on the photograph is another matter. By the way, the photographs are not for the public, so, therefore, that purpose could not be served by these photographs. But I am aware that in the future, of course, that could play a role in order to give the public the right impression of what this case is about. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that image into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, this photograph is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you tender just the photograph or would you like to have the marking in evidence? I can imagine after what I said that you're a bit hesitant. Feel free to tender whatever you want to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think that with the marking if it's -- if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, but the first one got a number without a marking, so then we have to attribute another number to the mark --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The second -- a second exhibit, if Your Honours please, with the marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then, Madam Registrar, that would be -- the marked photograph would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked photograph would be Exhibit number P20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the other one, then, is not tendered so that remains marked for -- or was it admitted already? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have them both admitted, to keep matters short.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you were describing this episode where the soldiers came to the house and kicked the door in, and you described how they were dressed and so on. Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Idriz Balaj, a.k.a. Togeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you recognise him? Did you see his face or through other means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a very brief period of time, he wore the mask back.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He raised his mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you able to see his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your house have electricity at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think earlier in your evidence, you mentioned torches. Did torches provide any light?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any electricity, but each and every one of them had a very strong flashlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you notice any features about Toger's face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw his face very well. He read a piece of paper. I don't know exactly what he read, but I remember that he directed the flashlight on that piece of paper, and that enabled me to see his face very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see his features -- sorry, let me withdraw that question. Did you see the area around his nose and mouth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see the area around his nose and mouth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first he raised his mask halfway. Then after a little while, maybe five seconds or ten seconds, not more, he raised his mask up and I could see the entire face.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you notice any features about his face, any unusual features?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the upper lip, he had a sort of scar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, If Your Honours please, the witness indicated an area to the right of his upper lip with his thumb, I noticed, as he gave that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we confirm Mr. Di Fazio's observation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's an observation of this kind and if no one responds, then it's on the record. And I take it -- if it would be incorrect, I would have corrected it. That's the way I used to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I wasn't in a position to see that. That's my difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. Of course, I'm better placed to do that. But it's correct, what Mr. Di Fazio said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your sister leave the house with the KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did she freely leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they took her at the time. She was -- she had her hands tied behind her back and she was crying. Togeri was holding her by her right hand, and she was crying and she was not in a good condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember what she was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was wearing black clothes and a leather jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I've heard what you said about the need for photographic evidence. However, in this case, I would like to show one more photograph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, it will be under seal, and it's an image that should not be shown to the public. It won't take me long to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- if you give the number to Madam Registrar, then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown 65 ter 684.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be, Madam Registrar ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
