utterances.text: Who is that person, Witness? And don't mention names. Rather, let me rephrase the question so that you don't need to do that. You've been referring to, just now, evidence of a sister being taken away and also earlier in your evidence of a sister M. Is that sister M?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Also in your evidence just now you mentioned that when she was taken away, she was wearing black clothing. Is that the black clothing she wore? Again, if you're not sure, please don't try and give an answer. Just tell us that you're not sure. I don't want you to give us anything other than reliable evidence concerning her clothing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had black clothing that looked like this. I see here she had a wristwatch and a bracelet, and then I don't remember what she was wearing on her foot -- feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I tender the image, the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Therefore, it's admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you see your sister again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only when we saw her dead after some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Approximately how long after her -- this episode when she was taken away by the soldiers did you see her dead body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately a week later, as far as I remember. It was about a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where did you lay eyes upon her dead body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day when her body was found, I personally did not happen to be there, but she was found dead in the woods near Bardhaniq village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was one of your brothers involved in the recovery of her body? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And where did you actually see her? Or, in fact, did you see her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw her when she was at home, when they brought her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any wounds on her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That leather jacket that she was wearing, that jacket had about 50 or 60 traces of stabs and it also had traces of blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the jacket holed? Did it have holes apparently cut into it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The jacket that I saw had traces of blood and had many cuts from stabs, especially in the area around the neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from the jacket, did you actually look at any part of her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, she had an injury inflicted by a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. What injury? Where on her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the head, near the ear. It was an injury caused by a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you indicate to the Judges using your finger where you saw this wound near her ear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably here, around the ear area, but I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know if my colleague from the Defence saw that, but for the purposes of the record, I say that the witness indicated an area to the back and just behind his right ear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you just turn around and show Defence counsel where the wound you observed was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this part here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you please also tell us whether it was the ear that you are pointing at now, or it was the ear you were pointing at earlier? Because initially you pointed at your right ear and now you're point -- do you know which ear it was or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just described the area, I didn't mention whether it was the right or the left ear. But as far as I remember, it was the left ear. When I saw this, I was very young. I was scared. But to my recollection, it was the left ear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Please continue, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Following the discovery of sister M's body and these events you've just spoken about, did your family remain in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We no longer remained in the village. We saw what was going on and we were forced to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I want you to explain that expression to the Trial Chamber. You said "... we were forced to leave." Now, what exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we found the body of my sister, we buried her the next day and we immediately left the house. We no longer lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just on a -- very briefly, where precisely did you bury her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of our house, maybe 50 metres away from the house, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've told us that you left after you buried your sister and that you left the house the next day immediately, so we know what you did. But what we want to know is something more, we want to know why you left. Why did you leave the house? Now, it may be obvious to you, but I want to hear your words. I want to know exactly why you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because a lot of things befell on us. Every now and then a member of my family would be taken away, would be -- would disappear, would go missing, or killed, so we were scared to continue and live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm now approaching the end of my examination-in-chief. There's just a couple of -- two more topics that I need to very briefly address.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned a town, a little -- small village nearby, called Irzniq or Rznic, a matter of some kilometres away, and earlier in your testimony you said that there was a headquarters there, a KLA headquarters there. Did you ever go there to that headquarters in company with members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And, Witness, at the very beginning of your testimony, you told us about an episode involving a shooting and a car, a red Lada, you mentioned, and an episode --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- in which one of your brothers was involved. Do you know if the police investigated that episode?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there when this incident was investigated. I don't remember; therefore, I cannot say anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if you were there; I'm asking you this: Do you know if the police investigated this episode?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/19 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably the police investigated this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, at the beginning yesterday I mentioned a document to you concerning a report. I know from having spoken to Mr. Guy-Smith that I believe there is no objection to the tendering of this report and I would therefore now like to tender into evidence this particular document, and it's 65 ter 1193. I don't need to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct. He may want to attempt to refresh the witness's recollection about the use of the document. I don't know, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't intend to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I simply want to tender it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want to tender it from the bar table?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: From the bar table. The witness has given evidence about certain matters that you can read within the document and the Prosecution's submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's to corroborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's to corroborate his evidence and it speaks for itself, and that that's sufficient basis for putting it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know the document. Should it be tendered under seal? Does it identify anything that should not be identified? I've got no idea but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It does so resoundingly, so it should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P22, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any of the other Defence counsel objecting to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to it being tendered. It is a document that contains a certain amount of unsourced conclusion and Your Honours will bear that in mind in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see Mr. Harvey. So, therefore, there's no objection. It is then -- before we decide to admit it, let's first have a look at it, so, therefore, a decision will follow on admission. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, anything further?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Witness, thank you very much for answering my questions. If Your Honours please, that concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Perhaps it would be a good idea to have the break first and then start cross-examination. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm in total agreement because, among other things, there's some technical difficulties that we're actually having at our station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, I suggest that we first ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'll have a break, Witness 19, and after the break you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence, at least that's what we expect at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine with me. No problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I just deliberated for a second with my colleagues. We get the impression, either right or wrong, that you would think that we could, on the basis of this testimony, draw any conclusions as to the identity of the person the witness has described as being frequently present and perhaps also to draw conclusions as to whether this person is identical to one of the accused. If I summarise the evidence at this moment, we see that a person is described -- a person is given a name, is known by a certain name, a name which may be identical to the name of one of the accused, but the Chamber has heard no evidence until now which would allow for the conclusion that that person bearing that same name would be the same person as one of the accused. I don't know whether you -- for example, one of the -- one of the -- what the Chamber, under normal circumstances, would accept -- would expect is, for example, a recording of an identification on the basis of a photo-spread or, well, whatever. Therefore, the Chamber wonders -- of course, we are in a position to call whatever evidence. If it would be -- if we correctly have the impression that you'd consider that we could draw certain conclusions, we might encourage you to review that -- whether that -- whether our impression -- whether your position, if our impression would be right, whether your position would need to be reviewed or whether the Chamber, who's, of course, not in a position to -- we can call for further evidence on the basis of -- you see, sometimes if a question does not fully clarify an issue, we might ask one or two additional questions. We have now heard a long testimony of this witness until now and we just wonder -- of course, it could be that later in the case, that you come with evidence which clearly demonstrates that the identity of the person this witness has described could not -- I don't know what evidence there's still to come. I mean, we're in the beginning of the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but if you would -- and that if you would be of the opinion that this, well, would create a chain which allows for the kind of conclusions the Chamber could imagine the Prosecution would ask us to draw at the very end, then I think that you should think about that carefully. But, of course, again we cannot speculate on what evidence is still to be expected by other witnesses. It could be well that there's no problem whatsoever. I mean, finally, you present your case, and we do not know exactly what you will present to us and how you will present it to us. I add to this immediately that courtroom identification is not considered a reliable way of resolving the matter I just raised, so, therefore, if you are thinking about that, it might not be the best thing to then consider, to resolve it in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I just indicate that Mr. Re has formally communicated to me that the Prosecution's position is it will not be seeking any courtroom identifications in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I just established that there's no other identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This witness, if Your Honours recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- mentioned that he knew Toger as Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There will also be other evidence in the case that the Prosecution says will lead to the inescapable conclusion that there was one Idriz Balaj and one Toger, and they are one and the same person in the area during the relevant time frame of the indictment. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that all. I take it that the issue is that you have asked ten times to this witness whether he had seen the face of that person, whether -- so, therefore, the most obvious way of establishing, at least that's the obvious way if you want to establish that that's one of the accused, is to find one way to see that -- whether this person, from which he heard that he introduced himself by the name of Toger, that he said he further sought to find out who this person was and he heard the name of Idriz Balaj. That's -- everything's fine still. And I wouldn't say that on the basis of other evidence that you could not -- but, of course, the first thing that you would think of, under those circumstances, if I've seen the face of a person, well, then to try to find out whether he recognises what he has seen at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, this is, I would say, basic -- basics in identification theory, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But we're not going to -- I didn't intend to lead any sort of sort of dock identification in this particular instance, and one of the reasons has been referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, okay, that's clear, then. We will adjourn until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Di Fazio, in relation to some observations I made before the break, has ever a photo-spread been shown to this witness, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we understand this as that -- did you verify whether that had ever been done, or do you just know whether it was ever done?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've not made active inquiries to check out what I believed to be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What I understood, I was satisfied with my understanding. I never made further inquiries, I think, of the sort that Your Honour is raising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Re, would you like to add anything to what Mr. Di Fazio just told us? I mean, it might be that you have other knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not as I stand here. There is something I would add. I read the transcript - I wasn't in court - where Mr. Emmerson said I had formally communicated to him there would be no dock identification in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The communication is a matter of -- the expression "doc. identification" is a matter of degree. The Prosecution's view is there may be cases of recognition where it would be permissible for the Prosecution to ask a witness if they recognise someone, but it's a matter of degree. We would not intend to ask someone to identify one of the accused on the basis that they had met them for a very brief period, once in their life or something. We understand the highly limited value of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it ever comes to identification procedures or recognition, whatever you call it, in court, that should be properly introduced, and the Chamber will decide whether or not it will allow any such thing to happen, knowing the full details, then, of which witness, what he's supposed to recognise, what has been done before in this respect. So, therefore, it's on the record now that you do not fully subscribe to what Mr. Emmerson said, and the Chamber adds now that it should be -- notice should be given well in advance with all details.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was going to be my suggestion because, as Your Honours, I'm sure, are well aware, there is considerable learning and research on that subject. And if there were to ever come a point where the Prosecution's position in any way changed, then one would need to have time to assimilate that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But as I understand it, and again just for the record, Mr. Re does not demure or in any way dissent from the statement that I am recorded as having made; namely, that there would not be attempts to identify witnesses in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I also indicate that I did inform my colleagues from the Defence during the break that if ever there were to be a situation where we were to seek to lead recognition evidence in court, we would, of course, notify them, as Your Honour has just ordered us to, in advance as to the circumstances and when we were going to do it. And, of course, the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So I put on the record that if we were, we, of course, would notify them in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the standard literature, such as the book by Professor Wagenaar, is well known by everyone. Then may the witness be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does the Trial Chamber require my presence for any administrative or for other matters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you wait for one more, two more minutes, then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 19, I have one question for you, not about the events at the time but a totally different matter. You have given a couple of interviews. You are now testifying in this courtroom. Was ever, during any of these interviews, was ever a piece of paper shown to you with the pictures, the photographs, of several persons where you then were invited to point at persons you mentioned during your interview? Did that ever happen? Do you have any recollection of such a thing to have taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean? For what persons or -- I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then be -- I'll try to do it on a more general level, but was there ever a series of pictures shown to you where you were invited, for example, to see whether you would recognise Toger or Togeri or Mr. Balaj among these photographs? Was ever such -- was that ever shown to you? Apart from whether you were able to do it or not. I mean, that's not the question. Did it ever happen that they showed you a series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us when it happened? Was that here in The Hague, or was that in ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Later? You say "later." Could you tell us when --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- when was it? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2005, I think, or 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then where were you when such a series of photos were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you point at someone on these series of photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, with respect to a person I recognised who is called Toger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So my question, quite simple, was: Did you point at any person, whether right or wrong? Did you point at any person when these photos were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I pointed at one person in a photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember who was present? I mean you said it was in Kosovo. Was this an interview by -- by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were two persons or three who asked me to talk with them, and I asked them what they wanted me to talk about, and then I talked to them later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that -- were these the people where you signed a statement with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we have received several statements given by you, some of them in 2004, July 2004 and the 20th of October, 2004, and we have a statement of an interview that was held in October 2005. Do you remember that you were interviewed three times? Let me see if ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do remember very well. From 2004 to 2005, I know that I have given interviews and such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it -- you said 2005. Was it during the last interview in Kosovo that you were shown these photographs or was it one of the earlier --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in the last one. In the first, I think, interview during 2004, I was shown these photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you asked whether your presence was still required and I said wait for two minutes. I take it that you now are aware of a matter that might need to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Clearly, it needs to be clarified before the witness finishes his testimony. If Your Honours could excuse me, I can go and make the relevant inquiries. It's very difficult for me to do it from where I'm sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If I might, with regard to the general issue of photo identification and the specific issue asked by the Court. I initially wrote a letter to the Prosecution on the 10th of January concerning the issue of photo identification because of a series of concerns I had with regard to that. I received response to that letter on January 25th and on the 6th of February. Both of those letters are in the e-court system and can be released for your review. The importance of those letters is that the response very clearly indicates the witnesses who photo identification procedures have been used with, and it says specifically on page 2, "photo identification procedures have been used in respect of ten potential witnesses who will be listed on our witness list. They are," and then it proceeds with who they are. This particular gentleman is not one of them. The other person that we were referring to is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That also clearly appears from his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It causes me some -- it does cause me some concern that if, in fact, such a procedure did occur, because to be perfectly honest with you, my examination was predicated upon a different premise, I'd like to know, and obviously as quickly as possible, whether or not there is such a record, whether it did, in fact, occur, and would ask the Chamber's indulgence potentially for the purposes of further cross-examination, which is something I'd rather not do because I'd like to keep the trial going. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do understand. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness put his headphones on again. Thank you. Witness 19, the Chamber has a few more questions on these photos shown to you. Do you remember how many photos were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately ten small photographs. They were all together on a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you asked exclusively whether you recognised Toger, or Togeri, or were you asked also whether you recognised other persons on these photo-series?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These photos showed Toger, but there were other persons but I didn't recognise the other persons. That's why I recognised only him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You only recognised Toger, and that's what you told the person that interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you given much time to look at them? Did you have to respond quickly? Did they say, We'd like you to tell us within a minute whether you recognise him, or were you given ample time, well, let's say, 10 or 20 or 30 minutes, to look at the photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had time until I recognised the person, and until that time I said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you asked to put something on that piece of paper or were you just asked to point at the photograph? I mean, could you tell us in more detail what exactly happened? Did you have to -- were you given a pen to put a cross at the photographs you recognised or were you just asked to point at ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, I know that I indicated at the photograph I recognised and then we continued with our talk about other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was this at the beginning or at the end of the interview? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, it was at the beginning, when we started the interview. In 2004, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you have any recollection on was it two rows of photographs, small photographs, or was it three rows or was it -- do you remember, more or less, how that piece of paper looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember how many rows there were, but I remember that there were several photos -- small photos lined up. I cannot tell you how many rows there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if you would please look at me at this moment. If I look at a piece of paper, I can look at it like this, you see, and then you'd expect all the small pictures to be like that and look at it so. Another way of putting pictures on a piece of paper is to do it like this, so you have then -- then they are lined more broadly. Do you remember whether you looked at the photos like this or whether you looked at the piece of paper like this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, it was normal format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Like this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, I always -- one is landscape and the other is -- portrait. Yes, yes. The witness confirmed that he looked at the piece of paper in portrait format, rather than in landscape format. Did they say anything to you about, Well, well done, this is the right -- or did they say -- did they comment in any way when you had pointed at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was shown the photographs. I looked at them. I told them, This person resembles him, and then they said, It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any recollection on that photograph? Was it just faces or could you say -- could you see also part of the clothing of the persons that were in the photographs? Was it the same for all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photos were small and I could see from this part up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're showing approximately from shoulder and above. Could you see anything about, for example, whether they were dressed in civilian clothing or in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you discussed with them why, in your statement which you signed, nothing was said about these photos shown to you and the person you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what to say about this not being mentioned in the statement. I guess that's not my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not blaming you in any way for anything. I just wondered -- of course, it's not your duty to draft the statement, but I can imagine that you would have raised the issue and said, Well, you read it to me, but you didn't read anything about the photos. Whether you raised it or not is not your mistake, but did you? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We mentioned it. I looked at the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you mentioned it. What exactly do you mean by that? Because my question was about whether, when your statement was read to you, whether you said anything about the absence of any reference to the photos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the Chamber will consider whether it chooses at this moment to use its right to call witnesses in relation to this procedural issue. Could you inform the Chamber whether the persons who did the 2004 interviews are still employed by this Tribunal or by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The interpreter is certainly here. I can make inquiries of the interpreter. The investigator isn't. There are two further pieces of information, if Your Honours could ask the witness, it would certainly assist me, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: One is where the interview took place. A related one took place in the Pristina field office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The witness has at this moment has his -- could you take your earphones off again for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Firstly, where the interview occurred; and, secondly, if he could describe the people who -- who interviewed him. That would identify for me, as best as I -- very clearly, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, what we know is -- I earlier in private session said something about photo-spreads. Looking at presentation of another photo-spread, it would not surprise the Chamber if it would be the October interview. And, of course, for the October interview, we know where -- but we'll verify that with the witness in a second. I think, as a matter of fact, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: October 2004 or 2005? There's a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think, again if we look at the other information, I think that would be 2004. If I remember well, that was the 21st of October, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it's 2005, the investigator is still here. If it's 2004, the investigator does no longer work at the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If it might be of any assistance, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- the specific investigator in question gave a declaration with regard to the issue of his performance as it related to giving photo-spreads on January 29th of 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my information, would that information confirm any photo-spread to be shown to the witness who's in front of us at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would not. The interpreters involved in the October interview, Mr. Re, are they still employed? I'm now talking about -- let me just -- yes, I think that would be Artan Grubi and Maklen Misha.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, they both still work for the Tribunal; one here and one in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which one here and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Maklen Misha.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is he in any way involved in interpreting in this case at this moment? I mean, apart from interpreting in pre-trial, but at trial? I mean, could it be that he has followed the whole of this discussion at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do believe he's been involved in some of the proofing sessions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We only have, I think, two Albanian interpreters so there's a high degree of probability that -- we only have two who can assist us in Albanian proofing, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is inclined to use its power to call witnesses and to do that immediately in relation to one of the interpreters, but we'll not decide any of these matters before the parties have had an opportunity to comment on this intention. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It would greatly assist us and maybe facilitate any decision you make if the Trial Chamber could ask the witness where the interview occurred and who was present in which the photos were shown to him. I might be able to find an answer fairly quickly one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just ... Defence, any comments on Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. I'm guided by the Chamber's concerns. The interpreter who was involved in the interviews of the 20th and the 21st of October dealing with the respective witnesses is also the individual who was involved in the proofing of the witness who is presently before us. So I think -- just so you have that particular piece of information. The investigator who was involved in the statement-taking of both of those witnesses is the investigator, that is, a Mr. -- and I don't believe I'm breaching any problems by mentioning this gentleman's name, that's Mr. Lorenzo-Quiroz, Q-u-i-r-o-z. He gave a declaration with regard to precisely what he did concerning photo-spreads on, as I said before, the 29th of January of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm guided by the Chamber's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we have a direct source of knowledge available --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That could be of some great assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that could be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm a bit -- I'm a bit -- I'm a bit shocked, to be perfectly honest with you, in the context of the correspondence that occurred in regard to the issue of photo identification, including specific responses we received from the Prosecution in this regard, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not speculate on what -- let's first -- let's first focus on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. The only reason I'm raising that at this point is because I think it also might be of some assistance to the Chamber if at some point you were to take a look at the history of how this issue developed pre-trial, it may be of some assistance to you also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we are assisted by it, but let's first focus at this moment on ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll first follow the suggestion by -- but I'd first like to check everything in my documents; otherwise, I might put the wrong questions. Mr. Re, you suggested that we ask the witness where the interview was held. From the statements - they're not in evidence, but please correct me if I'm wrong - I see that place of interview for the 18th of July, 2004 and the 20th of October, 2004 and the 9th of October, 2005 interviews are all Pristina field office, Kosovo. So if we try to identify which of these interviews, the witness said already that it was in Kosovo. Why do we learn from putting the question to this witness where it was held? Because then we still have three options.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are two things I need to know. One is where the interview occurred, whether it was in the field or in the office. The second one is if he could describe what the interviewer looked like, perhaps by nationality, then I could probably narrow it down to when it occurred. The other two pieces of information I need to make the relevant quick inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if an interview says that the place is Pristina field office, would that mean that it would be an office building in Pristina or could it be anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, it will be the UNMIK office where the ICTY has a floor in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: However, it may well be there's another document which we haven't located. I just don't know, nor the date. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're now referring to possible statements given --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at -- not reflected in the witness statements we have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't know. I just don't know and I can't answer without that information. Some photo ID was done with witnesses not at the Pristina field office, it was done in their homes, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if I could identify the nationality of the investigator, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, if you can make a comparison --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then, of course, there's some likelihood of it being done in the Pristina field office, which is at least the location known to this Chamber, although not in evidence, but on the basis of the information received until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A location where once a photo-spread, perhaps of a similar nature, was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. Mr. Re indicated that if he could identify the nationality of the investigator, then I assume he was going to proceed with -- you could figure out where to go and how to get ahold of him. This issue is very clear. There is no doubt about who it is. He knows precisely who it is, and it is the gentleman who is contained on the statement, Mr. Lorenzo-Quiroz, the very gentleman who has received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have -- of course, we have one -- the locations for the several interviews are recorded as the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I know precisely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: However -- however, the interviewers are not the same persons, so it might make some sense to ask the witness whether he could describe the interviewer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- could the witness ... Witness, we apologise for perhaps not bothering you with the matter, but at least you need a lot of patience. May I ask you, this interview where these photos, as you told us, were shown to you, could you describe -- let me first ask you: During all these interviews, were the persons who interviewed you, were they the same persons or was -- or were these different persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my knowledge, there were two persons when I gave my statement. It wasn't an interview; it was a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But now you have given three statements. Do you remember whether at these three occasions you were interviewed by this same person, or was it any of these occasions, was there a different person interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, I spoke with two persons during the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that two persons were present when you were interviewed or do you intend to say that at one of the interviews there was a person other than at the other interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, that's the way it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Different persons at the other interview; is that -- because I gave you two options.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps could you please describe the person who was interviewing you when these photos were shown to you. Was it a man? Was it a woman? Age? Colour of hair? If you don't remember, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of them, I know that he had dark hair, black hair. It was male.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Age, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 30 years old, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, does it give a clue already to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, because I need to -- there were two persons. Whether the person was the interpreter or the investigator, and was it in the same office or did they go somewhere else? There's a possibility that there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that would be a new subject, whether there's any unrecorded further interviews. But when these photos shown to you, where was that? You said in Kosovo, but could you be a bit more precise? Did you go anywhere? Was it at your home? Was it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In an office, not at my home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In which town or village or city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When these photos were shown to you, were there two persons putting questions to you? Of course not at the same time. But there was a couple, two, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, one, just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one. Were there interpreters present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we were discussing things, when the interview was in progress, only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And at any other moment were there more interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter was only one. It wasn't allowed to use two interpreters at one same day, there was no need for two interpreters on the same day. While during another interview, there was another person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- do you still remember, when these photos were shown to you, do you remember who was the interpreter? I can imagine that you wouldn't remember anymore, but do you happen to remember who was the interpreter when these photos were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, would the interpreter by the name of Maklen Misha, would that interpreter be at this moment somewhere in this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could that interpreter be located without further explanation on why we want the interpreter to be located?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The deputy chief of investigations, Mr. Reed, has already sent a message to those surrounding him not to notify him what's going on. I've got an e-mail to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's any way of having this interpreter in this courtroom -- do you think there's any possibility? I mean, if you're in the building, it usually takes you a couple of minutes to get here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would like to call this person as a Chamber witness in order to clarify this procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is Your Honour intending to do that as in now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. If Your Honour can excuse me, I might be able to, as an officer of the court, make the arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I take it that without any further explanation, you will try to get the witness in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, we'll consider how to proceed with the present witness. Witness 19, you may have noticed that there's an issue about these photographs which the Chamber would very much like to clarify before we continue with cross-examination by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber intends to excuse the witness for the day and to ask him to come back tomorrow. I do not hear any objections, so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 19, we'd like to clarify the issue with you, perhaps a small portion. That will take us some more time, and it will certainly take us all the time remaining today. Therefore, we'd very much like you to come back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in Courtroom III, because we're sitting in a different courtroom tomorrow. You will then be -- most likely you'll be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'd like you -- one second, one more second. I'd like you, as I did yesterday, I'd like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony that you have given or are still about to give. And our apologies for not being able to proceed as we had in mind for today. Madam Usher, would you escort the witness out of the courtroom once he has received my words in translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Everything is okay with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber suggests that due to protective measures in place for the witnesses that the witness which is now called will testify in private session, but it is not the intention of the Chamber to keep this testimony, in its essence, private. We'll consider that but -- of course, also depending on what the testimony will be. But we'll certainly consider later to make, if not all, then large portions of the testimony public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn most likely for a very short period of time. We'll see whether the witness is located, whether the witness is available, to testify at this very moment, and we'll resume as soon as that's clear. --- Break taken at 1.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please inform the Chamber sitting this afternoon in this courtroom that we'll have a delay. Then I'd like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.06 p.m.,
